Now technical and design decisions: Let's list them properly, as an array of strings:

1. Rabbit sink batching will use a configurable batch size (default 100 per U5) with a optional flush timer to prevent indefinite batching for low-throughput scenarios.
2. The Gradle module build option will be implemented as a custom Gradle plugin that applies the Spring Boot plugin with MODULE layout scoping, and sets Spring XD dependencies to provided scope automatically.
3. HDFS acceptance tests will use Testcontainers to spin up ephemeral HDFS instances for CI, avoiding reliance on external test infrastructure.
4. Compression support will be implemented via a pluggable strategy interface, with GZIP as the default codec, allowing users to inject custom codec implementations via Spring's dependency injection.
5. Baseline benchmarks will use JMH (Java Microbenchmark Harness) and run on identical hardware and with the same test workload as previous baseline runs to ensure performance comparison validity.
6. The DB disable option for DIRT runtime will be implemented as a runtime configuration flag that conditionally skips DB component initialization, without modifying core stream processing logic.
7. The RxJava processor core interface will extend RxJava's Flowable interface to align with reactive stream standards, and will implement the standard Spring XD processor contract for stream processing.
8. All new features will be backward compatible, with existing configuration options and APIs remaining unchanged to avoid breaking existing user implementations.
